title: Approximation property of the chosen dimension
statement: For each natural number $q$, put $\alpha=1/(q+2)$ and let $t$ be the standard Gaussian upper-tail quantile of mass $\alpha$. There is a dimension $N$ such that the upper-tail indicator of the normalized sum of $N$ uniform signs has mean within $\alpha/2$ of $\alpha$, and its level-one Fourier weight is within half the square of the standard Gaussian density at $t$ of that square; the dimension index chosen for $q$, plus one, has this property.
